surfaceForm: the University of Luxembourg (Q5.1 questionbox: "The University of Luxembourg is a small institution")
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with the role-based term "the institution" / "a small institution" as the subject of the comparison objection.
rationale: Names the University of Luxembourg directly as the institution being defended. The objection structure (small institution vs MIT/Stanford) is generic; only the named institution must be parameterized.

surfaceForm: University of Luxembourg (Q3.4 questionbox: "neither RESTENA nor the University of Luxembourg publishes any Science DMZ today")
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to "the institution" / "our institution"; this whole Q&A is a Luxembourg-specific local-deployment objection.
rationale: Direct naming of UL inside the objection text; the entire Q3.4/Answer pair is a country-and-NREN-bound argument.

surfaceForm: the University of Luxembourg's current infrastructure, contracts, and staffing (Q9.1 answer)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with "the institution's current infrastructure, contracts, and staffing".
rationale: Cost analysis is anchored to a specific named institution; the role (the adopting institution) is what matters, not the name.

surfaceForm: the University of Luxembourg's existing Committee for Reasonable Adjustments (Q6.2 answer: "has not devolved into a mechanism for bypassing academic standards")
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to "the institution's existing reasonable-adjustments committee (or equivalent)"; the precedent is the existence of such a body, not the specific UL one.
rationale: Cites a UL-specific internal committee as precedent. Many institutions have such bodies; the argument should reference the generic mechanism with an optional local instantiation.

surfaceForm: RESTENA / \gls{restena} (appears throughout: Q3.4, Answer Q3.4, Q5.1, Q9.1, Q9.2, summary table, \gls{restena}-\gls{csirt})
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with the role term "the national NREN" (National Research and Education Network) and "the NREN CSIRT".
rationale: RESTENA is Luxembourg's NREN. The architecture argument relies only on the existence of an NREN providing GEANT access and a CSIRT; the specific NREN is jurisdiction-bound and must be parameterized.

surfaceForm: \institution{ULHPC} (Q3.4 answer, twice)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role term "the institution's HPC facility / HPC team".
rationale: ULHPC is the University of Luxembourg HPC centre — a named local facility. The argument needs only "an HPC facility moving petabyte-scale traffic".

surfaceForm: \institution{MeluXina} (EuroHPC) (Q3.4 answer); also in summary table Q3.4 row
location: argumentation-body-EN.tex, sec:q-autonomy (Answer to Q3.4) + sec:summary table
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to "a national/EuroHPC supercomputer" or parameterize as the regional EuroHPC system.
rationale: MeluXina is Luxembourg's EuroHPC supercomputer. Country-bound named facility; the role is "the national EuroHPC system".

surfaceForm: \institution{LIST} and \institution{LIH} (Q3.4 answer: "RESTENA, the University, LIST and LIH co-design a federated research-network zone")
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to "the research-active institutions in the national ecosystem" / "peer research organisations and a biomedical research institute".
rationale: LIST (Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology) and LIH (Luxembourg Institute of Health) are Luxembourg-specific public research bodies named as mutualisation partners. The role is generic national research partners.

surfaceForm: the Department of Computer Science, the SnT Centre, and the \gls{hpc} team (Q9.1 answer, Step 2 pilot)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to role-based "entities with the strongest domain expertise (e.g., a computer-science department, a security/research centre, and the HPC team)".
rationale: SnT is the University of Luxembourg's Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust — a UL-specific named centre. Department of Computer Science and HPC team are UL-internal units used as the named pilot scope.

surfaceForm: Country/jurisdiction binding: "binding law in the EU and in the Council of Europe member states (including Luxembourg)" (Q6.3 answer)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise the parenthetical to "(including the institution's jurisdiction)" or parameterize the country.
rationale: Explicit naming of Luxembourg as the binding jurisdiction. The legal argument (EU Charter/ECHR binding) is generic across EU/CoE members; only the country anchor is local.

surfaceForm: "a Luxembourg-specific pattern" / "Luxembourg's scale" / "the realistic form for Luxembourg" / "Luxembourg has not done X yet" (Q3.4 answer, multiple)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace each Luxembourg reference with "the institution's national context" / "a small-ecosystem pattern" / role-based small-jurisdiction framing.
rationale: Repeated country naming embeds the argument in Luxembourg. The underlying claim (small research ecosystem, limited engineer pool, no NSF-CC* equivalent) is generic to small national systems and should be parameterized.

surfaceForm: "no European equivalent to the NSF CC* programme" / absence of an NSF-CC*-style national funding route (Q3.4 answer)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise to "the absence of a dedicated national research-network funding programme comparable to the US NSF CC*"; this is a jurisdiction-bound funding assumption stated as if universal.
rationale: Implicitly assumes the institution's country lacks an NSF-CC*-style programme — true for Luxembourg/EU but not a universal premise. Should be framed as a per-jurisdiction condition rather than a stated fact.

surfaceForm: "central-IT spend on the order of USD 1,600 per student FTE" and information-security spend percentages 8-15% / 3.6% benchmark (Q9.3 answer)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the sourced sector benchmarks (Gartner/EDUCAUSE) as generic, but flag the per-student-FTE figure as a currency/jurisdiction-bound reference the adopting board reads against its own enrolment and budget.
rationale: These are sourced sector statistics (cited), not UL-specific. Per the project's abstract-over-quantitative-self-references rule, sourced statistics are retained. Flagged only because the USD per-FTE figure is currency-bound and presented as a sizing anchor; generalisation is optional, not required.

surfaceForm: ICRADP / \gls{icradp} and "CARPN" (section title: "Questions on the ICRADP (Independent Commission for Reasonable Adjustments; fr: CARPN)"); Q6.1, Q6.2, Q10.2
location: argumentation-body-EN.tex, sec:q-carpn (section heading + Q6.1/Q6.2 boxes) and sec:q-meta (Q10.2)
proposedGenericDecision: The ICRADP is a suite-specific invented governance body. Retain as a defined construct of the policy proposal but ensure the gloss/acronym is suite-neutral (the French "CARPN" form ties it to a Francophone jurisdiction).
rationale: ICRADP is the proposal's own named mechanism (the English acronym is generic), but the parenthetical French acronym CARPN assumes a French-language jurisdiction. Keep the body; parameterize or drop the language-bound acronym.

surfaceForm: "the governing bodies" / "the board" / "the board cannot decide" / "a board still needs an order of magnitude" (Q9.3 question + answer)
proposedGenericDecision: Already largely role-based ("governing bodies", "board", "CIO"). Confirm these remain generic governance roles rather than a specific board-of-governors/rectorate shape.
rationale: Uses generic governance roles (governing bodies, board, CIO) — already institution-agnostic. Flagged for confirmation only: no UL-specific governance shape (rectorate, board of governors) is named here, so no change needed.

surfaceForm: "the Digital Policy Commission" (Q2.1, Q2.3, Q2.4, Q6.x, Q8.1, Q9.1, Q9.3 — the proposal's governance body)
location: argumentation-body-EN.tex, multiple sections (sec:q-governance, sec:q-carpn, sec:q-regulatory, sec:q-costs)
proposedGenericDecision: This is the proposal's own named governance construct (role-based, not UL-branded). Keep as a defined suite-wide term; verify it is named identically across the suite.
rationale: Digital Policy Commission is an invented, role-descriptive governance body internal to the proposal, not a UL-specific organ. Institution-agnostic already; flagged only for cross-suite naming consistency.

surfaceForm: "its statutory security obligations, including those under NIS2" and "For a public university ... Article 6(1)(e)" (Q8.3 answer); assumes the institution is a public body subject to national NIS2 transposition
proposedGenericDecision: Generalise the lawful-basis argument to "a public-sector or public-interest institution"; note that the NIS2 statutory duty depends on national transposition (stated here without naming the transposing law/country).
rationale: Implicitly assumes the institution is a public university whose GDPR Art.6(1)(e) public-interest basis and NIS2 statutory duties flow from national transposition. Public-vs-private status and the transposing instrument are jurisdiction-bound and should be parameterized rather than assumed.

surfaceForm: Named university incidents used as evidence: Paris-Saclay, Western Sydney, Texas Tech, Rennes (Q1.1, Q7.1, Q7.2)
proposedGenericDecision: Retain as evidential precedents (Layer 4/5 empirical incidents) — these are external, sourced examples, not the adopting institution. Keep, as they are part of the generic evidence base usable by any institution.
rationale: These are third-party incident precedents (cited evidence), not specificity tying the document to UL. They generalise to any institution adopting the architecture. Flagged for awareness only; Rennes/Paris-Saclay are French and could be supplemented but need not be dropped.

surfaceForm: Reference-university roster: MIT, Stanford, Cambridge, Oxford, ETH Zurich, CERN, Michigan, EPFL, NC State, Penn State, Wisconsin-Madison, Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne (Q1.3, Q2.3, Q5.1, Q5.3, conclusion)
proposedGenericDecision: Retain — these are external comparator institutions forming the convergence/precedent evidence base, reusable by any adopting institution. Not UL self-reference.
rationale: Comparator institutions are the generic evidence layer (institutional precedents) and are explicitly intended to be transferable. They do not bind the document to UL and should be kept.

surfaceForm: \institution{...} and \gls{...} macros expanding to UL/LU-specific terms: \gls{restena}, \institution{ULHPC}, \institution{MeluXina}, \institution{LIST}, \institution{LIH}
proposedGenericDecision: Audit the shared glossary/\institution definitions so that the localisation variables above resolve these macros to role-based generic terms (NREN, HPC facility, EuroHPC system, national research partners) for the suite build.
rationale: Several macros (gls/institution) expand to Luxembourg-specific named entities. Genericising the document requires the macro expansions themselves to be parameterized at the glossary level, not just the prose.
